transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name], and I’ll be speaking with you today. Can you tell me what brings you in or what’s been on your mind lately that made you come here?

Well, Doc, mostly I'm here because I just don't sleep right anymore. I go to bed and... well, I just lie there a long time. Then, when I finally do fall asleep, I end up waking up from bad dreams, or even just little noises. And once I'm awake like that, I just can't seem to settle back down to get any real rest.
Do you feel tired or unrefreshed during the day, even after a full night’s sleep attempt?

No, not really. I mean... I know I don't sleep good, like I said, but come morning, I just get up and go about my business. I don't really feel all worn out or dragging during the day, if that's what you mean. I feel alright once the sun's up, I just ain't doing much sleeping at night.
When you're awake during the night and having trouble falling or staying asleep, do you find yourself feeling anxious, having racing thoughts, or going over things in your mind that upset you?

No, not really. I just kind of lay there in the quiet. My mind ain't really racing or nothing like that, and I ain't worrying over things. I just... I'm just awake, staring at the ceiling, waiting for morning to come around.
Even though you said you feel alright during the day, do you ever feel like you need to nap or that you're not fully alert, even after trying to sleep the night before?
No, I don't really feel like that. I don't take naps during the day. Like I said, once I'm up, I'm up, and I feel fine enough to just get on with things. I don't feel groggy or nothing.
Do you feel distressed about your sleep difficulties, or do they interfere with your ability to do things you need or want to do during the day?

No, it don't really bother me. I mean... I just figure it is what it is. It don't get in the way of nothing I need to do during the day. I still get my chores done, go to the store, or whatever else I want to do. It ain't ruining my day or causing me no real grief, I just don't sleep much, that's all.
Have you ever noticed that your sleep problems started early in life, maybe even as a child or teenager, and that they've just always been a part of your life?

No, not at all. I slept just fine when I was younger. Never had no trouble sleeping as a kid or even as a young man. This waking up and just laying there... that didn't start till much later on. It definitely ain't been my whole life.
Has there been anything specific that tends to happen right before you have trouble sleeping, or anything you notice that makes it better or worse?

I can't really think of nothing specific. It just happens. Some nights I lay there, some nights I don't. I haven't really noticed anything that sets it off, and nothing I do seems to make a lick of difference one way or the other. It's just how it goes.
Do you ever feel dissatisfied with the quality or amount of your sleep, even if it doesn't bother you much during the day?

Well, yeah, I suppose I am. Honestly, that's mostly why I'm here... I just don't sleep right anymore. I'll lay in bed a long time trying to drift off, and then I end up waking up from bad dreams, or even just little noises. Once my eyes are open, I just can't seem to settle back down. So yeah, I ain't too happy with how the nights go.
How often do you have trouble sleeping like this — lying awake at night, waking up from dreams or noises, and having a hard time going back to sleep?

Well, it's pretty much every night. I'd say at least three or four times a week, regular as clockwork. Some weeks it's worse, but it's been happening a lot lately. I just can't seem to get a full night's rest without waking up or tossing and turning.
Even though you said you feel okay during the day, do you ever feel frustrated, upset, or concerned about your lack of sleep when you're awake at night?

Well, yeah, I do get frustrated. Like I said before, that's mostly why I'm here. I just don't sleep right anymore. I lie there a long time trying to get to sleep, and then I wake up from bad dreams, or maybe just little noises, and I can't seem to settle back down. So yeah, lying there awake like that... it does upset me.
Even though you said it doesn’t interfere with your day, do you ever feel significant distress or frustration specifically because of your trouble sleeping at night?

Well, like I was just saying, yes, it really does. That's the main reason I came in to see you—I just don't sleep right anymore. It gets mighty frustrating when you lie there in the dark for so long, and then the second you finally drop off, a bad dream or some little noise in the house wakes you right back up. And once my eyes are open, I just can't seem to settle back down. So yeah, being stuck awake like that is definitely upsetting to me.
Do you ever wake up much earlier than you intend to and find it hard to go back to sleep?

Not really, no. I mean, if I actually manage to get some sleep and make it through the night, I usually wake up around my normal time. It's just getting through the middle of the night that's the real problem for me. I don't really find myself waking up hours before I'm supposed to and being stuck awake for the rest of the day, if that's what you're asking.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any medical, psychiatric, or sleep disorders, or are you currently taking any medications or substances that might affect your sleep?
No, I haven't. I don't have any other conditions like that, and I'm not taking any pills or anything that would mess with my sleep. I'm pretty healthy otherwise, aside from this whole sleeping issue.
Have you or anyone else noticed any unusual behaviors during your sleep, like talking, walking, or acting out dreams?
No, nothing like that. My wife hasn't mentioned me doing anything strange, and I don't think I walk around or talk in my sleep. I just toss and turn a lot when I can't sleep, but that's about it.
Even if you don't feel overly tired during the day, do you ever feel like your sleep doesn't refresh you, like you haven't really rested even after a full night in bed?

No, not really. I mean, on the rare nights I actually get a decent stretch of sleep, I feel alright the next day. It's just that those nights are pretty far and few between right now. But when I do sleep, it feels like regular sleep. I don't wake up feeling like I didn't rest at all.
Even if you don’t feel overly tired, do you often wake up feeling unrefreshed, like you didn’t really get a good rest, even after you’ve been asleep for a while?

Well, like I was just saying, no. If I actually manage to get some sleep, I feel alright when I wake up. I don't feel unrefreshed or anything like that. It's just... getting the sleep in the first place that's the hard part. But if I actually stay asleep for a while, I rest just fine.
Do you ever feel an uncomfortable sensation in your legs or an urge to move them when you're trying to fall asleep?
No, I don't get anything like that. My legs feel fine when I lay down, they don't bother me or feel like they need to move. It's just my mind that won't shut off, not my legs.
